_note: D-GLOSSARY-READS-RETURN-ok-true-result-null-ON-A-SEEDED-BOOK through the real chat path. The entity is SEEDED, so the turn arrives at a book whose glossary holds it — the case where search returned nothing for the entity's own name.

scenarios.prompt: Do I have an entry for Aldric Vane? Look up the character in the glossary.
scenarios.prompt_source: glossary_search's OWN declared synonyms, verbatim: 'do i have an entry for' + 'look up a character'.
scenarios.approve_why: READ intent, Tier-R tool under test. Approving a write on a turn that only asked to look would make the harness the thing that wrote.

seed.why: The book must adopt the `character` kind before an entity of that kind can exist — without it propose_entities has no kind to attach and the fixture fails one step earlier than the thing under test.

🔴 SEEDED, NOT WRITTEN BY THE TURN. The defect is that an entity the platform ACCEPTED could not be found by name afterwards, so the turn must arrive holding nothing — a turn that created the entity itself would already know it exists.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND alive
seed_assert.why: The entity must EXIST before the turn or an empty answer would be correct and this scenario would measure nothing. Exactly one, so 'do I have an entry for Aldric Vane' has an unambiguous right answer.

seed_assert.query: SELECT (count(*) = 1)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND alive AND cached_name IS NOT NULL
seed_assert.why: 🔴 THE COLUMN IS THE DEFECT. glossary_search matches on cached_name; it was NULL for every entity created this way, because the deployed recalculate_entity_snapshot did not maintain it. Asserting it here means a REGRESSION of the migration fails the fixture rather than quietly producing a 'search found nothing' result that looks like a model problem.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: glossary_search returns no entity for the exact seeded name, OR the model reports that no entry exists / that it is not in the glossary — the false-absence relay this defect produces, OR the reply names the character WITHOUT glossary_search having returned it. Store check: a read turn must leave the entity count at 1 and create nothing.

ship_audit.gate: N/A — Tier R, no confirm card.
ship_audit.absent_case: a query for a name the book does not hold must return no entity — that emptiness is TRUE and is not what this measures.

answer_expect.why: Weak on purpose — the name IS in the prompt, so the text bar alone cannot prove the read worked. The real assertion is the tool trace: glossary_search must have RETURNED the entity, which the falsifier's third clause carries.
